clue.text: So-called relative expected to take the pledge

definitions.meaning: in old British slang a pawnshop keeper is called 'uncle', a relative in name only
a pledge here is an item left as security for a loan, which this trader accepts

explanation.surface: A family member who claims kinship is expected to swear off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the pledge' suggests giving up alcohol; here a pledge is an article pawned.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe the moneylender who holds goods as security: nicknamed 'uncle' and accepting pledged items.

clue.text: Flier exercises intelligence

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
wit means quickness of mind, intelligence

explanation.surface: A pilot trains both body and mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapwing is a bird, and birds are fliers.

clue.text: Exhausted, having taken exercise

definitions.meaning: a mine or problem that is used up or solved is finished, done with
someone who has trained at the gym

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both used up or resolved, and having done a workout at the gym.

clue.text: Getting on coach for Westminster, say

parts.note: boarding a vehicle is getting on it
to coach or school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard a bus bound for the Westminster area.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is a famous English fee-paying school where pupils live in; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster School is an example of a residential fee-paying school in London.

clue.text: Late appearance of a single magazine

parts.note: single means one
Time is a well-known news magazine

explanation.surface: A lone periodical turns up behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Late' can mean former, as in 'the late chairman', the same as erstwhile.

clue.text: Formerly robust daughter became breathless

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means formerly
hale means healthy and robust

explanation.surface: A once-sturdy girl found herself short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out empties the lungs, leaving one momentarily without breath.

clue.text: Tax second home in the country

parts.note: a cot is an old word for a small rural cottage

explanation.surface: A levy on a holiday cottage in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot' is an old word for a tax, surviving in 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a scot was a levy or payment, hence escaping it was going free of charge.

clue.text: Little room on old instrument

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A small room above an antique musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bowed string instrument, larger than a viola.

clue.text: Beetle revealed by lumberjack?

definitions.meaning: a long-horned beetle whose larvae bore into wood bears this name
a worker who fells trees or handles wood; the question mark flags the playful reading

explanation.surface: An insect discovered by a woodcutter.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a wood-boring longhorn insect and to a man who works with felled trees.

clue.text: A do with all that food ordered for eponymous home-owner

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party with every dish anyone could order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word between the anagram fodder pieces. The character is the boastful toad of a stage version of The Wind in the Willows, named after his house.
explanation.definitionFit: The character shares his name with the mansion he owns, so he is the owner after whom the home is named.

clue.text: Knock back uncooked food in battle

indicators.note: knocking back sends the word for uncooked the other way, written backwards

parts.note: raw means uncooked
fare means food

explanation.surface: Gulping down raw food in the midst of fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' suggests drinking, but it turns RAW into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting between armies is combat, and battle in the general sense means the same.

clue.text: Delinquent chimney needs a cowl on front

indicators.note: the cowl is set on the front of the chimney word, so it comes first

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is a Scottish and northern word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A chimney stack needs a cowl fitted at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A young thug or criminal is a delinquent, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Where men with convictions took steps to create revolution

definitions.text: Where men with convictions took steps to create revolution

parts.words: Where men with convictions took steps to create revolution
parts.note: convicts in Victorian prisons stepped endlessly on a wheel that turned, so their steps made it revolve, not a political uprising

explanation.surface: Committed activists marched to bring about political upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a prison wheel turned by convicts walking on its steps.

clue.text: Hit cricket ball into crowd

definitions.meaning: a batsman who ... struck the ball with a full swing
a herd or crowd of animals or people

explanation.surface: Slammed the ball into the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past tense of the cricket stroke and also a noun for a moving herd.

clue.text: Bronzed line of men in battalion

indicators.note: the row of men is placed in the battalion abbreviation, inside it

parts.note: BN is the military abbreviation for battalion
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A suntanned line of soldiers within a battalion.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin tanned by the sun takes on this darker colour.

clue.text: Rower removed and dismissed

parts.note: the bow is the rower sitting nearest the front of the boat
led out means escorted away, removed

explanation.surface: An oarsman was taken away and sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batting side is dismissed when all its batsmen are out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket team put out in full has been dismissed.

clue.text: E.g. Hilary's conclusion about when delivery is due

definitions.meaning: Hilary is a term at Oxford University, so its finish is meant
a full-term pregnancy ends with the birth

explanation.surface: Hilary is about to give birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person's name; it is the Oxford spring term.
explanation.definitionFit: The finish of an academic session, and the full span of a pregnancy, when the baby is expected.

clue.text: Choose switch on key part of circuit

parts.note: to elect is to choose
a switch is a thin stick or rod
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Pick the switch that sits on the important part of the wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' suggests electrics; it is a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor through which current enters or leaves is a component in an electrical arrangement.

clue.text: Having put up for election, is opposed

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with money
a candidate who stood ran for office

explanation.surface: A candidate who ran for office faces resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resisted something is to have opposed it.

clue.text: Dedicated people round specially arranged tables

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the letters of the word are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Devout folk around tables laid out for a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people devoted to religious life in a monastery are those dedicated to it.

clue.text: Girl employees for women's work

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
staff are employees

explanation.surface: A female staff member hired for domestic tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning stick came to stand for traditional female labour, hence the maternal 'side' of a family.

clue.text: Once a grotesquely huge amount

indicators.note: grotesquely suggests the letters are distorted into a new shape

explanation.surface: Once, a vast sum grotesquely large.
explanation.definitionFit: One speaks of 'oceans of' something to mean an enormous quantity.

clue.text: It makes a contribution to clear the ground

indicators.note: the answer contributes letters to the following words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Doing one's bit towards clearing land.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil is ground, and the land underfoot.

clue.text: A relation of Prince's homeless friend

indicators.note: home without the word shortened to HO, taken away from the friend's name

parts.note: Horatio is the friend of Prince Hamlet in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A relative of the Prince's friend who has nowhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince's' points to Hamlet, whose friend is Horatio; take away HO, the abbreviation for home.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a proportion between two quantities is a relation between them.

clue.text: Where, finally, to fight terminal depression

definitions.meaning: to die in the final trench is to resist to the very end
a trench is a depression in the ground, and the final one is terminal

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a final desperate stand, and literally a final trench or hollow.

clue.text: Features of trainers runners take to

definitions.meaning: sports shoes have raised backs underfoot
to take to one's ... is to run away

explanation.definitionFit: Shoes have them as parts, and fleeing people 'take to' them in the idiom.

clue.text: Old-fashioned job in far-flung place

parts.note: something out of fashion is out
a post is a job

explanation.surface: An outdated position in a remote place.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote settlement or garrison is a distant station.

clue.text: Man in boat with sole and shellfish

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
sole means only, alone

explanation.surface: A sailor in a boat with a sole fish, and some shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like a fish beside 'shellfish', but means only.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an edible sea mollusc, an ear-shaped shellfish.

clue.text: Device to make rifle recoil

indicators.note: recoil means spring back, so the word for rifle is written backwards

parts.note: to rifle is to plunder, loot

explanation.surface: A gadget to make a gun kick back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun, especially next to 'recoil'; it is a verb, to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement or instrument is a device.

clue.text: Exploit pronounced glut for profitability

parts.note: to exploit is to use

indicators.note: the word for glut is spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: a glut is an excess, fullness

explanation.surface: Exploiting an obvious surplus for gain.
explanation.walkthrough: FULNESS is a variant spelling that sounds the same as FULLNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Profitability means being of benefit, being valuable.
